summary: Live-traffic rehearsal and safe revert guidance for tenant adaptive optimizer flags
description:
Issue summary: Customer (VeloxAI, Dedicated) reports intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes and increased token cost after enabling an experimental adaptive optimizer bundle (dynamic batching + aggressive KV prefetch + mixed-precision quant profile). They want a safe plan to rehearse live-traffic changes and an atomic rollback procedure that minimizes tenant disruption.

Impact: Elevated tail latency (95p) from ~320ms to ~860ms for conversational endpoints, increased per-token cost by ~18% on observed traffic mix, some requests experienced streaming disconnects. No full 5xx incident but user-facing slowdowns and elevated error counts for long-session chat flows.

Environment: Dedicated pool, tenant pinned to model rw-inference/gpt-medium-8b-quant, autoscale enabled, routing policy: region-first with fallback to smaller-quantized variant. Change rolled out as feature-flagged optimizer bundle on 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Tenant route /v1/chat stream with typical user session distribution (avg length 240 tokens, tail 1k+).
2) Enable adaptive-optimizer profile "velox-experiment-03" which sets batch_coalesce=aggressive, kv_prefetch=on, quant_profile=mixed-2bit, async_batching=enabled.
3) Observe tail latency and stream disconnect logs over 30-90 minutes.

Observed behavior: Tail latency regresses on multi-session conversations, occasional partial streams where clients see truncated deltas (client-side resumes succeed). Memory pressure alerts on two nodes with elevated GC churn. Autoscaler triggered new nodes but traffic sticky routing kept some sessions on overloaded nodes.

Expected behavior: Modest latency improvements for batchable short requests, no regression for long-session conversation tails and stable streaming.

Temporary workaround attempted by customer: toggled kv_prefetch=off and reduced batch_coalesce to conservative. Partial improvement but cost still higher than baseline.

Request: Assistance with a safe rehearsal procedure (shadow/replay or traffic-shift), a stepwise failback that can be executed with minimal traffic disruption, and a checklist of telemetry to validate before/after revert. They also asked for a lightweight preflight that can be run in staging to replicate tail behavior.
investigation_notes:
Initial SRE findings: 1) Telemetry shows interleaved long sequences create large KV cache churn when kv_prefetch is on with mixed-2bit quant because eviction heuristics weren't tuned for long sessions. 2) Aggressive batch coalescing increased queueing latency for sessions waiting for batch formation under this traffic mix. 3) Node-level memory pressure correlates with model variant that uses larger KV value sizes in mixed-2bit path. Hypotheses: a) Incompatible eviction/kv window sizing for long sessions; b) batching thresholds too aggressive for high-variance sequence length.
Actions taken so far: pulled heap/swap and per-process memory snapshots, collected sample request traces (trace ids attached in comments), validated that fallback model variant responds successfully when traffic split to it. Suggested next step is to run a canary rehearsal with 5% live traffic and an immediate 0.5x conservative-batching profile for the same tenant to compare delta. Also recommended a snapshot of optimizer flags (feature-flag snapshot id ff-velox-20260309) prior to any change.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use VeloxAI tenant in dedicated pool. 2) Apply optimizer profile velox-experiment-03 to the tenant route. 3) Stream chat sessions with mixed short + long sequences for 60 minutes. 4) Observe tail latency in console per-route 95p and check node memory alerts. 5) Revert flags to baseline and compare metrics.
logs: Attached: console trace excerpts (trace ids: t-20260309-7f2c, t-20260309-9a1e), node memory snapshots: node-12-heap-20260309.log, agent telemetry dump: telemetry-velox-20260309.json. Key log lines indicate 'kv_cache_evict:thrashing' and 'batch_coalesce:wait>200ms' correlated with the slow traces.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Collecting traces and asking SRE to pull memory profiles. First response ETA within 4 hours.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Diego Ramirez (SRE): Confirmed memory pressure on nodes 11-13. Found eviction thrash with kv_prefetch enabled. Proposing a staged rehearsal plan: 1) snapshot current flag state, 2) deploy conservative-batching to 5% traffic, 3) monitor 95p for 30m, 4) if safe, increment to 20% and run for 1h.
2026-03-10 11:27 - VeloxAI (customer): Can we rehearse with replay tooling instead of real traffic? We prefer no user-visible slowdowns for now.

2026-03-10 11:36 - Diego Ramirez (SRE): Rehearsal options: a) Traffic replay on a shadow cluster (recommended) with same distribution; b) Live 5% canary. Shadow replay requires a staging cluster sized to match peak working set—we provided sizing guidance. Both approaches will include an automated abort if 95p or error rate crosses thresholds.
2026-03-11 08:50 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer opted for shadow replay. Provided replay checklist and script. Next steps: schedule replay window and SRE to observe metrics.
proposed_rehearsal_plan: 1) Take feature-flag snapshot ff-velox-20260309. 2) Provision a shadow cluster with same model variants and KV sizing as prod (min nodes=3 for this tenant). 3) Run traffic replay for 2 hours using the customer's anonymized request traces for at least one high-variance window. 4) Compare per-route 50/95/99p latency, token cost, stream disconnects, node memory and eviction counters. 5) If deviations exceed safe thresholds (95p > 20% regression or error-rate > 0.5%), abort and collect diagnostics. 6) If rehearsals are acceptable, perform a live 5% canary with conservative batching profile and automated rollback.
safe_rollback_checklist: 1) Snapshot current optimizer flags and recording ff id. 2) Prepare a rollback playbook with exact flag values to restore. 3) Ensure route-level traffic split capability and route sticky-session draining steps. 4) Pre-create a quick rollback CLI command (rwi rollback-optimizer --tenant velox --snapshot ff-velox-20260309). 5) Define automated abort criteria on console and pager (95p increase >20%, error spike >0.5%, memory OOM alerts). 6) Communicate a 30-minute quiet window with customer for rollback execution. 7) Post-rollback validate 95p and token cost against baseline for 60 minutes.
resolution: Pending rehearsal completion and SRE validation. Follow-up: schedule shadow replay and then canary; target resolution after successful rollback test or acceptance of conservative profile.
